transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-12
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Windward Head of ML), Samuel Ortiz (Windward Infra), Greta Liao (Windward Product), Tomás Vega (Windward SRE)
---
Auto-summary (auto): Align on POC success metrics (p95 latency < 350ms for 16k tokens, cost target <$0.035 per 1k tokens for gen paths), capture token distribution, plan replay and benchmarking steps.
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time. this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. quick roll call then i'll hand off to diego.
[00:08] Priya Nair: thanks, priya here — head of ML at Windward.
[00:12] Samuel Ortiz: sam, infra.
[00:15] Greta Liao: greta — product.
[00:17] Tomás Vega: tomás, oncall/sre.
[00:20] Diego Alvarez: diego here, i'll run the technical bits and the benchmark plan.
[00:25] Maya Chen: perfect. goal for today is scoping a POC: we want to characterize traffic, agree success criteria, and map a pilot timeline. if we can get the token mix + a replay hookup we can run two baseline benchmarks — steady-state and burst. sound good?
[00:39] Priya Nair: yes. our main ask: make sure we don't regress quality while hitting latency and cost. we'll need to see end-to-end numbers with our prompts.
[00:48] Diego Alvarez: totally. quick clarifying q: is Windward planning hosted Redwood or private VPC for the pilot?
[00:55] Priya Nair: ideally VPC, because of PII considerations. but for the first replay we can do hosted with scrubbed data if needed.
[01:03] Maya Chen: noted. we can do an initial hosted replay to iterate faster then replicate the same workload in your VPC — that mirrors our usual flow.
[01:11] Samuel Ortiz: scrubbed data is ok but we need to ensure traffic shape matches production — qps spikes and concurrency are non-trivial for us.
[01:21] Diego Alvarez: can you give ballpark numbers? what are your steady QPS and peak burst?
[01:26] Samuel Ortiz: steady is about 12 rps, average concurrency about 8, but we see spikes to 320 rps during billing windows — short 30s to 2m bursts.
[01:36] Greta Liao: and token lengths vary — routine requests are 90–120 tokens out, but some report-generation flows push 6k+ output tokens.
[01:45] Priya Nair: note: many long outputs are streaming; we care about tail latency for first token and mean throughput for streaming.
[01:53] Diego Alvarez: ok that helps. for sizing we need: qps distribution (percentiles), concurrency histogram, input token histogram, output token histogram, and ratio of streaming vs non-streaming requests.
[02:06] Maya Chen: i'll add a template in the workbook for those histograms.
[02:10] Tomás Vega: one thing — our infra adds a 50–80ms network hop for VPC-hosted endpoints, so Redwood numbers will be slightly optimistic. please annotate.
[02:19] Diego Alvarez: good call, tomás. we'll report raw server-side times and end-to-end numbers.
[02:23] [02:30] Diego Alvarez: next, success criteria — what does Windward need to consider this POC a win?
[02:34] Priya Nair: three things: 1) functional parity — outputs must match our quality thresholds vs current model (we'll supply eval prompts), 2) latency SLOs — p95 first-token < 350ms on typical queries and p99 < 800ms for non-streaming, 3) cost — target unit cost below our threshold (we'll share numbers) while also enabling autoscale for bursts.
[02:54] Maya Chen: can you share the cost ceiling as a number? that helps us evaluate quantization/variant tradeoffs.
[03:00] Priya Nair: aiming for <$0.035 per 1k generated tokens across average mixes.
[03:06] Diego Alvarez: ok. based on that, we'll propose two model configs to try: a lower-quantized variant for cost-sensitive routes and a higher-fidelity variant for long-form generation. we'll include dynamic routing rules in the Playbook.
[03:22] [03:30] Samuel Ortiz: about burst handling — how does Redwood do graceful degradation if capacity saturated? do you fall back to smaller model or queue?
[03:37] Diego Alvarez: we have automatic routing policies: preference order to cheaper variants, and a fast fallback model. for hard SLOs we can configure pre-warmed dedicated capacity or a hybrid reserved pool for the pilot.
[03:46] Greta Liao: i want to make sure quality gating is included — if fallback triggers we want visibility and a metric that flags quality drops.
[03:52] Diego Alvarez: we'll tie quality regression alerts to your eval set and surface diffs in the console.
[03:58] [04:10] Maya Chen: timeline proposal: week 1 (prep) — windward provides traffic samples + eval prompts; redwood provides workbook and initial config; week 2 (baseline) — hosted replay runs (steady + burst) and initial metrics; week 3 (analysis & tuning) — adjust batching/cache/quant profiles and run tuned replay; week 4 (VPC pilot) — replicate tuned config in VPC and validate. total ~4 weeks. is that feasible?
[04:35] Priya Nair: yes that's reasonable. we might accelerate if we can parallelize the replay and config tuning.
[04:40] Tomás Vega: we'll need the S3 share and replay tooling instructions asap.
[04:44] Diego Alvarez: we'll send a small Python replay harness and an S3 ingestion spec.
[04:49] [05:00] Priya Nair: question on metrics — can you capture per-token CPU/GPU utilization and kv-cache hit rates? we'd like to correlate token-lengths with GPU utilization.
[05:09] Diego Alvarez: yes, server-side telemetry includes per-request GPU ms, token-token breakdown, kv cache hit ratio, and concurrency traces. we'll provide a dashboard with per-route breakdowns.
[05:19] Samuel Ortiz: please include a CSV export, we ingest into our BI.
[05:22] Diego Alvarez: will do.
[05:25] [05:40] Maya Chen: ok capture: deliverables from Redwood are workbook, replay harness, baseline config, and a short Playbook with routing rules. from Windward we need token histograms, sample anonymized payloads, and success criteria + eval prompts.
[05:53] Greta Liao: on evaluation prompts — we'll share 120 seed prompts spanning short Q&A, multi-turn troubleshooting, and long-form report generation.
[06:02] Diego Alvarez: perfect. that gives us a quality matrix. we'll run automated evals after baseline and tuned runs.
[06:10] [06:30] Priya Nair: on privacy — can you confirm logs retention and KMS integration for the VPC pilot?
[06:36] Maya Chen: yes — for VPC we integrate with customer KMS, and logs are stored in their account; retention policy configurable. we'll attach SOC2 and encryption docs.
[06:46] Tomás Vega: bring the security pack; our legal/security team will scan.
[06:49] [07:00] Diego Alvarez: one more technical detail: for very long outputs (6k tokens) we recommend streaming with chunked KV handling; we'll include an optimized profile to reduce mid-output stalls.
[07:11] Priya Nair: that is key, some of our reports are generated in a single request, streaming helps UX.
[07:18] Maya Chen: any blockers?
[07:21] Samuel Ortiz: only that we need to anonymize and extract representative token distributions — we'll prioritize that.
[07:25] Greta Liao: i'm on the prompt set, will curate the 120 examples by monday.
[07:30] Priya Nair: i'll sign off on success criteria draft by tuesday.
[07:33] Maya Chen: great. we'll circulate minutes and the workbook tomorrow.
[07:36] [07:50] Diego Alvarez: brief on benchmark design: two primary experiments — (A) steady-state run at 12 rps for 30 mins capturing p50/p95/p99 first-token and streaming throughput; (B) burst replay simulating 320 rps spikes (30–120s) capturing tail latency and queue depth. also a long-output stress test with 100 requests of 6k tokens to validate streaming stability.
[08:13] Priya Nair: that maps to our concerns. what about warm cache assumptions?
[08:17] Diego Alvarez: we'll run both cold-start and warmed runs; prefix cache warmup steps will be documented.
[08:22] [08:35] Tomás Vega: for VPC we need a clear network diagram and egress rules.
[08:39] Maya Chen: we'll include an architecture appendix for the VPC pilot.
[08:42] [08:55] Maya Chen: ok final recap of next steps: redwood shares workbook + replay harness by 2027-08-14; windward shares anonymized traffic + prompt set by 2027-08-18; redwood runs baseline hosted replay week of 2027-08-24; tuning and VPC replication thereafter.
[09:15] Priya Nair: agreed. thanks all.
[09:18] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with the workbook and action items in email.
[09:22] Meeting ends.
